statement: S closed densely defined symmetric bounded below, deficiency(n,n)<∞, boundary triplet. For selfadjoint extensions H1,H2 the below-essential-spectrum counting shift σ=N_H1((−∞,λ])−N_H2((−∞,λ]) lies in[−σ−,σ+], where σ−+σ+=n−dim(L1∩L2).

statement: For selfadjoint extensions H0,H1 of one closed densely defined symmetric S with deficiency(d,d), D(i)=R1(i)−R0(i) maps into ker(S*−i), so rank≤d. For common z,w, D(z)=[I+(z−w)R1(z)]D(w)[I+(z−w)R0(z)]; the outer factors are invertible, hence the finite rank is anchor-independent. One compact resolvent implies both are compact.
verification_status: Elementary range/resolvent identity proof supplied; parent independently confirmed the rank strategy. No literature novelty asserted.
source_context: PAPER-D201 Theorem6.2,pp22–24 contains the source finite-defect mechanism under its semibounded setting; this proof does not assume semiboundedness.

statement: For compact-resolvent selfadjoint H0,H1 on the same Hilbert space, choose common real anchor c and suppose F=(H1−c)^−1−(H0−c)^−1 has inertia(p,m), rankr=p+m<∞. Define ξ(x) by N_H1((c,x])−N_H0((c,x]) above c and the negative difference on(x,c] below c. Then ξ(x)∈[−m,p] for all realx, with exact half-open conventions; ξ(v)−ξ(u) is the finite interval count difference. Hence |Δ_H1(K)−Δ_H0(K)|≤3r, Δ_H=N_H((2K,4K])−2N_H((K,2K]).
verification_status: Complete proof using both reciprocal branches and compact-tail inertia supplied; parent independently checked signs, endpoints, common anchor and3r cancellation. No separate third reconstruction or literature novelty claimed.
